title: basic-auth model-version read filter: judge each version object with _rm_or_prompt_read_predicate and cache the predicate per request
answers: Why can a user with a wildcard registered-model grant see prompt versions, or lose access to prompts they were granted?
Why is mlflowSearchRuns slow or doing many grant lookups for basic-auth users when runs include model versions?
Which predicate decides which model versions a user can read in GraphQL search results?
body:
Path: Model-version visibility in the basic-auth GraphQL path, covering the top-level `mlflowSearchModelVersions` result and the nested `run.modelVersions` list. Both go through `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._filter_model_versions_result` and `_post_resolve`, which use the helper `GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._model_version_read_predicate`.
Rule: Pass the whole model-version object to the predicate from `_rm_or_prompt_read_predicate(username)`, not the name with a registered-model predicate. Prompt versions are then judged by prompt grants, matching the REST `filter_search_model_versions`, and a registered-model grant (including `*`) does not reveal them. The predicate is memoized per request on the Flask `g` object, keyed by username, so one `mlflowSearchRuns` call builds it once instead of once per run.
Symptom: Prompt-version metadata could be revealed through a matching registered-model grant without a prompt grant, while prompts a user was granted were hidden. Each run in the runs table also triggered a user lookup plus a grants query.
Constraints: The per-request cache lives only for the current Flask request and is keyed by username. The filter is a no-op on data that was already filtered, so the second pass on top-level search is safe. Test: `tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_graphql_search_model_versions_judges_prompts_by_prompt_grants`.
applies: Visibility of model versions and prompt versions in basic-auth GraphQL responses, and any new resolver that filters model-version lists per user.
says: Searching runs is extremely slow when runs display associated model versions in the table.
Users with access to all models can see prompt versions they were never granted.
Prompt templates that were explicitly shared with a user fail to appear in search.
Separate prompt version visibility from registered model permissions across search and run details.
search: In basic-auth GraphQL authorization middleware, GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._filter_model_versions_result passes the full version object to _rm_or_prompt_read_predicate so prompt versions are evaluated against prompt grants rather than registered-model grants. The predicate is cached per request on Flask g by username to prevent redundant user and grant queries during mlflowSearchRuns when runs contain model versions. This prevents wildcard registered-model grants from exposing prompt versions, ensures granted prompts remain visible, and safely no-ops on already-filtered results. Applies to basic-auth GraphQL model-version filtering including mlflowSearchModelVersions, run.modelVersions, and any new resolver filtering model versions per user.
